showMoreRuns: {count, plural, one {Show # more run} other {Show # more runs}}
changeFailed: The change could not be saved. Try again.
openFolderDescription: Schedules and their run history are saved inside the folder you open.

allowHere.waiting: Switched on in this folder but not allowed on this Mac, so it does not run here. Allow it to run exactly as written below.
allowHere.changed: Switched on in this folder and changed since this Mac allowed it, so it does not run here until you allow it again.
allowHere.paused: Not allowed on this Mac yet, so Run now waits too. Allow it to run exactly as written below.
allowHere.noNextRun: Runs here after you allow it
allowHere.limit: at most {count} new documents per run

title: Automations
lede: Schedule recurring checks, then see what each run found. They run on this computer while Atlas is open.
malformedDescription: Atlas could not read the local schedule file and left it unchanged. Fix it, then refresh.
unavailableTitle: Atlas could not read this folder's schedules
unavailableDescription: Atlas could not read .ontology-atlas/rounds.json in this folder, so its schedules cannot be shown or run. Check the folder is where Atlas opened it, then refresh.

unrecorded.ledger: The run at {time} ended but could not be written to {file}, so it is not in this history. The schedule moved on to its next time. Check that this folder can be written to.
unrecorded.schedule: The run at {time} ended but its next time could not be written to {file}. Atlas keeps that time on this Mac until the file can be written. Check that this folder can be written to.

editWidens: This change lets the schedule do more than this Mac allowed. Saving allows the new version on this Mac.
noSummary: The run finished without a saved summary.
failedNoResult: The agent did not finish its reply, so this run left no result.
noAgentReview: No coding agent was ready on this Mac, so this review did not run. Open Agents to sign in, then run it again.
failedError: This run stopped on an error: {detail}. Run it again; if the same error comes back, open the folder again.
failedFolderNotRead: Atlas had not finished reading this folder, so this run checked nothing. Run it again in a moment.

undone.restored: Atlas put {page} back as it was before this run.
undone.removed: Atlas removed {page}, which this run had created.
undone.failed: Atlas could not put {page} back after this run. Open it and check it before you rely on it.

leftAsIs: {page} changed after this run wrote it; Atlas left it as is.
saveFailed: The schedule could not be saved. Nothing was changed.

runs.title: What it does
runs.body: The coding agent reads the ontology and its linked code, then proposes one small improvement.

when.title: When it runs
when.body: On the cadence you pick, such as hourly, every six hours or daily. A run missed while the app was closed runs once when it next opens.

writes.title: What it may change
writes.body: Nothing. You review each proposal and apply it on the map yourself.

sheet.title: Schedule an ontology check
sheet.description: At the chosen time the agent reads the ontology and code, then proposes changes. It writes nothing until you approve.
sheet.focusPlaceholder: concepts without a code location, stale capabilities, relation evidence…
sheet.focusHint: Leave it empty and the agent picks one small area from the current evidence.
sheet.mayRead: Read the ontology and current code evidence through the Atlas MCP server.
sheet.mayPropose: Describe proposed changes with exact slugs, paths, and uncertainty.
sheet.mayNeverWrite: Never write concepts, relations, files or approval records.

runs.title: What it does
runs.body: Checks that sources and wiki pages still match, and brings in changed documents from a connected service.

when.title: When it runs
when.body: On the cadence you pick, such as hourly, every six hours or daily. A run missed while the app was closed runs once when it next opens.

writes.title: What it may change
writes.body: Only sources and wiki page drafts inside the approved Library scope. Never the ontology.

runStopped: This run was stopped before it finished.

stage.note: It keeps running wherever you go in the app. Stop ends this run only; the schedule stays on.
stage.label: Run in progress

facts.runs: The coding agent reads the ontology and its linked code. An ontology check proposes one small improvement. A recheck rereads each concept whose code changed after its document.
facts.writes: An ontology check changes nothing. A recheck records, in the document of each concept that is still accurate, the commit it was checked at. It commits those documents and lists them under Run history, where one press undoes it.

sheet.description: At the chosen time the agent rereads each concept whose code changed after its document. Atlas records which documents are still accurate and commits them, so you can undo the whole run. A concept the agent finds out of date is listed with the agent's reason and left as it is.
sheet.limitHint: Between 1 and 25. The concepts that have waited longest go first; the rest wait for the next run.
sheet.mayRead: Send the agent each concept document and what changed in the files it cites.
sheet.mayWrite: Record in each document that is still accurate the commit it was checked at, as evidence_checked.
sheet.mayCommit: Commit those documents on the branch that is checked out when it runs, never on the remote's default branch. Atlas never pushes.
sheet.mayNever: Never change a sentence, title, kind, code location or relation, any other concept, or a file outside this folder.
sheet.cost: No agent run when no concept's code changed. Otherwise one agent run that reads up to {limit, number} concepts and at most {size} of text · at most {count, number} a day at this cadence.
sheet.noGit: This folder is not in a Git repository, so a recheck could not commit its changes or undo them. Open Git to make it a repository, then schedule the recheck.

recheck.summary: {checked, plural, one {# concept reread} other {# concepts reread}}: {accurate, number} still accurate, {outdated, number} out of date, {left, number} not decided.
recheck.waiting: {count, plural, one {# more concept waits} other {# more concepts wait}} for the next run.
recheck.skippedUncommitted: {count, plural, one {# concept was skipped because its document has} other {# concepts were skipped because their documents have}} changes you have not committed.
recheck.ignored: {count, plural, one {# answer named a concept that was not in this run, so Atlas ignored it.} other {# answers named concepts that were not in this run, so Atlas ignored them.}}
recheck.none: No concept's code changed after its document, so no agent ran.
recheck.noAgent: No coding agent was ready on this Mac, so nothing was rechecked. Open Agents to sign in, then run it again.
recheck.heldBranch: Not run: {branch} is the remote's default branch, and a recheck commits only on a working branch. Switch to a working branch, then run it again.
recheck.heldGit: Not run: Git cannot commit in this repository right now ({detail}). Finish that in Git, then run it again.
recheck.replyUnreadable: The agent's reply could not be read, so no document was changed. Run it again.
recheck.commitRefused: Git refused the commit: {detail}. Atlas put {count, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}} back as before this run and kept the new text in {copy}. Fix what Git reported, then run it again.
recheck.stopped: Stopped before it finished. No document was changed.
recheck.interrupted: Atlas closed during this run, so when it opened again it put {count, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}} back as before the run.

dialog.title: Recheck results
dialog.accurateLine: The agent reread this document against what changed in {files} and found nothing to change. Atlas recorded the commit it was checked at in the document.
dialog.leftLine: Atlas changed nothing, so this concept still counts as one whose code changed.
dialog.filesSent: Sent to the agent: what changed in {files}.
dialog.outdatedLine: The agent found text that no longer matches what changed in {files}. Atlas changed nothing, so this concept still counts as one whose code changed.

reason.noAnswer: The agent's reply did not cover this concept.
reason.changedMeanwhile: The document changed while the agent was reading it.
reason.refusedPath: Atlas does not send {path} to an agent, because its name says it holds keys or passwords or it lies outside this folder.
reason.cutUnread: What changed in {path} was too long to send whole and the agent did not read the file, so its answer was not taken.
reason.tooLarge: This document and what changed in its files are more than one run sends, so Atlas did not send it to the agent.

undo.done: {count, plural, one {Put # document back as it was before this run and committed that. It counts as a concept whose code changed again.} other {Put # documents back as they were before this run and committed that. They count as concepts whose code changed again.}}
undo.skipped: {document} changed after this run, so Atlas left it as it is.
undo.failed: Git refused the commit for the undo: {detail}. No document was changed. Fix what Git reported, then press Undo again.
undo.gone: This run's commit is no longer on this branch, so Atlas cannot undo it here. Open Git to restore a document from its history.

recheck.heldRefused: Not run: Git refused this schedule's last commit ({detail}). Fix what Git reported, then press Run now. The schedule runs by the clock again once a run commits.
recheck.headMoved: The repository moved to another commit during this run, so Atlas changed no document. Run it again.
recheck.commitHeldBranch: When the agent finished, {branch} was checked out, and it is the remote's default branch, so Atlas changed no document. Switch to a working branch, then run it again.
recheck.commitHeldGit: When the agent finished, Git could not commit in this repository ({detail}), so Atlas changed no document. Finish that in Git, then run it again.
recheck.commitRewritten: Git's hook changed {files} while committing, so the commit holds text Atlas did not write. The commit stays as it is: check it, and undo this run if it is not what you want.
recheck.offHere: This recheck came with the folder and was never allowed on this Mac, so it does not run here. To recheck here, remove it and schedule your own.
recheck.sent: Sent {size} of documents and code changes to the agent.

edits.factsWrites: An ontology check changes nothing. A recheck edits only the documents of concepts whose code changed, commits them, and lists every change under Run history, where one press undoes it.
edits.sheetDescription: At the chosen time the agent rereads each concept whose code changed after its document. Atlas records the documents that are still accurate, edits only the sentences that are not, and commits those documents so you can undo the whole run.
edits.mayWrite: Edit sentences in the body of those documents and record the commit each was checked at as evidence_checked.
edits.mayNever: Never change a title, kind, code location or relation, any other concept, or a file outside this folder.
edits.summary: {checked, plural, one {# concept reread} other {# concepts reread}}: {accurate, number} still accurate, {updated, number} updated, {outdated, number} out of date, {left, number} not decided.
edits.updatedLine: {count, plural, one {The agent changed # passage} other {The agent changed # passages}} after reading what changed in {files}.
edits.noMatch: The text the agent named is not in the body of the document, or is there more than once.
edits.heading: The agent asked to change a section heading, which a recheck never changes.
edits.tooMuch: The agent asked for more than {count, number} changes or a replacement longer than {length, number} characters. Rewriting a document is a conversation with the agent, not a recheck.
edits.notApplied: Applying the agent's changes would have changed something a recheck never changes, so Atlas applied none of them.
